description: Journal Bombay is your cozy all-day café in the heart of Santacruz, Mumbai, where coffee, culture, and conversations come alive. featured_reviews.name: Ishita Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place in Mumbai that quietly sets the bar ridiculously high for café dining, it has to be Journal.

Tucked in the lanes of Santacruz West, this spot feels like a hidden gem that you almost want to gatekeep — but it’s too good not to talk about.

Let’s start with the food — because wow.
I tried the Rigatoni Romesco pasta, and I’m not exaggerating when I say it has redefined what a good pasta should taste like for me. Perfectly cooked, rich, and balanced — the kind of dish you keep thinking about days later. The grilled artichoke & mushroom pizza was equally incredible — earthy, flavourful, and done just right.

What makes Journal stand out is that the food isn’t just good — it’s consistently thoughtful. The menu spans across multiple healthy and cheat options, so there’s always something exciting to try.  ￼
And nothing feels like filler — even the simplest dishes feel well-crafted.

The space itself adds so much charm to the experience. You’ve got both indoor and outdoor seating, and the outdoor section especially makes for a perfect brunch vibe. It’s relaxed, airy, and yes — there are quite a few cats casually strolling around, which somehow just adds to the whole personality of the place.

The vibe is exactly what you want from a café — calm, slightly buzzy, and very “slow morning energy.” It’s spacious, comfortable, and great whether you’re working, catching up, or just unwinding.  ￼

And the coffee? Absolutely holds its own. Smooth, well-brewed, and clearly taken seriously — which makes sense given it positions itself as a space for “coffee, culture & conversations.”  ￼

Service is warm and easy — the kind where you don’t feel rushed, and everything just flows.

Overall, Journal isn’t just a café — it’s an experience. One where the food genuinely impresses, the vibe grows on you, and you end up staying longer than planned.

If you’re someone who appreciates great food, good coffee, cozy corners, and a slow brunch done right — this one is an absolute must-visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

For dessert, we ended with Eggo, which had a waffle base topped with cream and strawberry – light, fresh and a perfect ending.
Overall, great food, unique theme and a must-visit cafe for Korean food lovers in Mumbai. Highly recommended!

I recently visited Aegyo Café, and it truly turned out to be one of the most charming and aesthetic cafés I’ve ever been to! The moment you step inside, the Korean-inspired ambiance instantly wins your heart — pastel décor, cozy corners, and such cheerful energy that lifts your mood right away. ✨

The staff was extremely polite and welcoming, and the service was smooth throughout our visit. Now coming to the best part — the food! Every dish we tried was beautifully plated, bursting with flavor, and carried its own unique twist.

We ordered the Chicken Yom Tom, Street Style Chicken Chilli, Chow Mein Bowl, and Pink Rice Bowl, along with Spring Rolls, a Belgian Chocolate Boba Shake, and a Strawberry Milkshake — and honestly, every single item was a hit! The Chicken Yom Tom had a comforting, mildly spicy taste that instantly stood out, while the Street Style Chicken Chilli was bold, tangy, and perfectly balanced. The bowls were hearty, wholesome, and packed with flavor — ideal for a fulfilling meal. 🍜

For desserts, we indulged in their Milk Cake, Assorted Mochi, and Churros, and it was the perfect sweet ending! The mochi was soft, chewy, and absolutely delightful — with just the right touch of sweetness. 🍡💖

featured_reviews.name: Mohak Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place recently and had a pleasant overall experience. The café has a very welcoming atmosphere with tasteful interiors and good music playing in the background, making it a comfortable spot to relax or catch up with friends.

I tried the Vietnamese cold coffee, which was decent but fairly average in terms of taste. The Korean cheese garlic bun, on the other hand, was excellent — soft, buttery, and nicely balanced with garlic and cheese flavors. Definitely the highlight of the order and something I would recommend trying.

I also ordered the mozzarella fries. While the texture was crispy and the portion was good, the seasoning felt a little mild and slightly low on salt. The dip served alongside didn’t complement the fries very well, which made the dish feel slightly underwhelming.

One thing that truly stood out was the service. The staff was courteous, attentive, and quick, which added a lot to the overall experience.

Overall, a nice café with a great vibe and good hospitality. With a few small improvements in seasoning and dip pairings, the food could easily match the quality of the ambience.

⭐ Rating suggestion: 3.8–4.0/5 (honest but fair)

Aegyo cafe was the perfect dine in spot for my Sunday dinner. Cozy vibes, perfect playlist and music loud enough to be enjoyed without having to scream across the table to have a conversation.

The food and service were bang on! We ordered the katsu chicken sando (YUM!), katsu curry (best I’ve had since my trip to Japan), miso ramen and long fries. The flavours were perfect and kept me going back for more. We paired this meal with their iced frappe and we couldn’t stop at 1. So good!

It instantly feels like a warm hug kind of place… perfect for catching up with friends, cute dates, or even a peaceful solo coffee + work day.

They’ve introduced a new Pan-Asian menu and I loved how comforting and flavourful everything tasted.

We tried
• Veg Shanghai – paneer lovers, this one’s for you! Tangy, saucy and super flavourful.

• Veg Gyoza – soft, nicely filled dumplings with a lovely dipping sauce. Simple yet so satisfying.

• Pad Thai Noodles – that sweet-tangy Thai flavour, nicely balanced with peanuts and veggies. Comfort in a bowl

• Chilli Garlic Fried Rice with Gravy – this was total comfort food! Spicy, garlicky and so wholesome when mixed with the gravy.

And of course… Boba time
• Lotus Biscoff Milky Brew is like dessert in a cup, rich, creamy and indulgent.

• Passion Fruit Boba is fresh, fruity and perfect if you prefer something lighter.

For dessert, we ended with their Strawberry Milk Cake and it was such a pretty and delicious end .. soft, moist and really fresh.

Overall, it’s a cute aesthetic cafe with good comforting food, great vibes and friendly energy. Definitely one of those places you’d want to come back to when you want something cozy and happy.

featured_reviews.name: Divya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dumpling Khang is a place I’ve been going to since 2019 — I still remember the first time I tried their chicken thupka and how much I absolutely loved it. It had this authentic, comforting flavour that made me come back again and again. For a long time, I used to order their momo-thupka combo on a monthly basis — and back then it felt totally worth it. It was around ₹170, came with a generous bowl of soup and 6 momos, and tasted super fresh.

Over time, of course, the price went up (₹190… ₹200… and now it’s ₹320-350 if you order online), but what’s more disappointing is that the quality has definitely gone down. The thupka still hits on some days, but the momos have become really average — they taste like pre-packed ones just deep-fried and served. Not the fresh, soft, flavourful momos they used to be.

There’s also this dish called Laughing — which they hype up quite a bit — but honestly, it was very underwhelming. It’s basically some kind of roll (reminded me of Gujarati khaman) with Maggi/Wai Wai noodles stuffed inside, and that’s it. For the price, it really doesn’t deliver.

We also tried their Nepali thali on our recent visit — again, something they highly recommended. But that was another miss. It had rice, basic dal, some greens, one sabzi (usually an aloo sabzi), a small portion of chicken gravy and achar. It was okay, not bad, but definitely not something I’d go back for.

Now coming to the space itself — it’s tiny. Like, four tables tiny. So only four groups (of 3–4 people max) can sit at a time. Because of that, if you go during peak hours, it gets super crowded and you may have to wait. And even after placing your order, the food can take a while to arrive. That said, the place does give off a very warm, comforting, homely vibe. It’s the kind of small place that makes you want to curl up with soup on a rainy day.

They also usually do these combo offers during New Year and other festivals — where you get a set number of dishes or momos for a fixed price. I’d honestly recommend that more than dining in right now. The combos are way more reasonable and they get delivered to your home, so you skip the waiting and the crowd.

So yeah — if you’ve never tried it, go for their soups. They still remind me of the flavours from Himachal. But otherwise, the rest of the food is average, prices are high now, and the overall experience just isn’t what it used to be.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ever since our office shifted from Mahim to Santacruz, this street-side stall had been on my must-visit list and I’m glad I finally got to eat here!

The service is super quick and the kebabs are served piping hot, straight off the grill. We started with the chicken seekh kebab, which was soft, juicy, and perfectly tender—definitely a highlight.

The mutton seekh kebabs, were a bit of a letdown. The taste was just okay and lacked that meaty punch you’d expect.

The bheja masala was creamy, rich, and absolutely delicious. The kiri was another winner—buttery, indulgent and full of flavour.

Gravies and kebabs are served with pav, paratha or naan.
Great food at throwaway prices, which is exactly what you want from a street-side gem.

Will definitely be visiting again to try more items from the menu!

Do yourself a favour and please try a plate of CHICKEN BAIDA ROTI which is so amazing that you might find yourself gulping it up all even before you realise.

If you like properly spiced and extremely generous portion of rice and soft chicken then the CHICKEN BIRYANI served here will keep you coming back for more.

CHICKEN RESHMI TIKKA was good in terms of texture and flavour combination.

CHICKEN KAATI ROLL was satisfactory.

So yes, drop by this humble eatery which is usually packed with family and friends happily tucking in as they offer tremendously delicious and mouth watering food.
